rows.source: function solve(n,edges){const degree=Array(n).fill(0),out=[];for(const[a,b]of edges)degree[b]++;const q=[];for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(!degree[i])q.push(i);while(q.length){q.sort((a,b)=>a-b);const u=q.shift();out.push(u);for(const[a,b]of edges)if(a===u&&!--degree[b])q.push(b);}return out.length===n-1?out:[];}

rounds.answer:
Context marker: INTERVIEW-113-79388915d92f9818.

The bug is in `src/core.mjs`, specifically `return out.length===n-1?out:[];`: a complete topological ordering requires exactly `n` vertices, not `n-1`.

A smallest valid counterexample is `solve(1, [])`. The sole vertex has indegree zero, so the queue starts as `[0]`; processing it produces `out = [0]` and empties the queue. The final check evaluates `1 === 0` as false, returning `[]`; the required result is `[0]`.
